# bnd

> A command-line client for Baidu Netdisk (百度网盘): list, search, manage, upload, download, share and save shares. One binary for macOS, Linux and Windows. Built to be driven by AI agents: `--json` output, meaningful exit codes, no prompts without a terminal. Human-readable output is Chinese; the JSON is language-neutral.

## Quick start

1. `bnd who --json`. If `loggedIn` is false, log in: `bnd login --cookies "BDUSS=…; STOKEN=…"` (or `--from-chrome` / `--from-edge`).
2. Inspect: `bnd ls --json <dir>` → `files[]` of `{path, name, fsId, size, isDir, md5?, ctime, mtime}`; `bnd meta --json <path…>`; `bnd tree --json [--depth n] <dir>` → nested `root.children`; `bnd search --json -r --path <dir> <keyword>`.
3. Act: `bnd download --json -o <local dir> <path…>`, `bnd upload --json <local…> <netdisk dir>`, `bnd mkdir`, `bnd rm`, `bnd cp`, `bnd mv`, `bnd share create`, `bnd share save`.
4. Read stdout: check `ok`, then the command's fields. For downloads take each file's absolute local path from `files[].file`; never build it yourself.

## Output

- With `--json` (before or after the command), stdout carries exactly one JSON document; progress and logs go to stderr. Keys are sorted. Times are RFC 3339 with the local offset; sizes are bytes; ids are exact integers.
- Every document has `ok` and `command` (e.g. `"share create"`). On failure: `error: {kind, message, exitCode, code?}`, where `code` is Baidu's error code when there is one (31066 / -9 not found, 31061 / -8 already exists, -12 wrong extraction code). Work finished before a failure is still in the document.
- `--help` and `--version` also answer with a document under `--json` (`help`, `version`).

## Exit codes

| code | error.kind | meaning | what to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | – | done | read the fields |
| 1 | failed | server, network or transfer failure | retry later |
| 2 | input | not found, already exists, no wildcard match, wrong extraction code, bad value | fix the input; `bnd ls --json` to look around |
| 3 | dependency | browser cookies unreadable (permissions) | log in with `--cookies` |
| 4 | auth | not logged in or login expired | `bnd login` again |
| 64 | usage | bad command line, or a confirmation needed without a terminal | see `bnd <command> --help`; add `-y` |
| 130 | cancelled | interrupted | rerun; transfers resume |

## Rules

- Netdisk paths are absolute (`/Photos/a.jpg`) or relative to the working directory set by `bnd cd` (`bnd pwd --json`). Quote them: they contain spaces, Chinese and wildcards.
- Wildcards `*`, `?`, `[…]` work in any path component and are expanded by bnd against what exists; a pattern with no match is an `input` error. A name that exists exactly as written always means itself (`"[1].txt"` is that file), and `\` escapes a wildcard character.
- `md5` is present only when it is the file's real content md5. Baidu does not know it for files stored in several blocks (typically those uploaded in 4 MiB pieces), so those have no `md5`.
- `mkdir` of a directory that already exists succeeds (`existing[]`), so it is safe to repeat.
- `cp`/`mv <src…> <dst>`: if `dst` is an existing directory, sources go into it; otherwise one source is copied/renamed to `dst`, several go into a new directory `dst`. `items[]` lists each `{from, to}`.
- `rm` moves to the recycle bin: `bnd recycle list --json` (`files[].fsId`, `daysLeft`), `bnd recycle restore <fsId…>`, `bnd recycle delete -y <fsId…>` (permanent).
- Downloads: `-o <dir>` (default: the `save-dir` setting). A directory downloads recursively into `<dir>/<its name>/…`; `--full-path` keeps the whole netdisk path. A file already on disk is `{"status": "skipped", "reason": "exists"}`; `--overwrite` replaces it. Interrupted downloads resume (a `.bnd-part` file sits beside the target meanwhile).
- Uploads: the last argument is the netdisk directory; the others are local files or directories (uploaded recursively as `<dir>/<name>/…`). If the target exists: `--policy skip` (default) → `skipped`/`exists`; `overwrite` replaces; `rsync` replaces unless the size is the same (`skipped`/`same-size`). `status: "rapid"` means Baidu already had the content and nothing was sent. Interrupted uploads resume.
- `files[].status` in transfers: `downloaded`, `uploaded`, `rapid`, `skipped` (`reason`: `exists`, `same-size`, `symlink` for a symlinked local directory, which is not followed), `failed` (with `error`); `summary` counts them. A path that cannot be read, or two files that would land on the same target, fail on their own while the rest still transfers. If any file failed the command fails, but the document lists every file.
- Shares: `bnd share create --json [-p <4 chars>] [--days n, 0 = forever] <path…>` → `shareId`, `link`, `pwd`, `url` (link with `?pwd=`). `bnd share save --json "<link>" [<code>] [--to <dir>]` saves someone else's share into the working directory (or `--to`); the code may be in the link. Saving your own share fails (Baidu: 文件已存在, code 2). `bnd share cancel <shareId…>`.
- Offline downloads run on Baidu's servers: `bnd offline add --json --to <dir> <url…>` → `ids`; poll `bnd offline list --json <id…>` (`status` 0 = done, 1 = running).
- `logout`, `recycle delete`, `recycle clear` and `update` need `-y` without a terminal. With no command and no terminal, bnd exits 64 instead of opening the shell.

## Command map

```text
Account   login · logout -y · who · users · su <uid|name> · quota
Browse    ls [-l] [--sort name|size|time] [--desc] · tree [--depth n] · meta · search [-r] [--path dir] · cd · pwd
Manage    mkdir · rm · cp · mv · recycle list|restore|delete|clear
Transfer  download [-o dir] [-p conns] [--overwrite] [--full-path] · upload [--policy skip|overwrite|rsync] · offline add|list|cancel|delete|clear
Share     share create|list|cancel|save
Other     config [set …|reset] · update [--check] [-y]
```

Settings and accounts: `config.json` in the user config directory (`bnd config --json` shows the path and the settings, never the cookies), or `$BND_CONFIG_DIR`.
